description:
We are STELLARCHIVE, a team of curious minds, creative thinkers, and aspiring innovators passionate about space exploration, technology, and storytelling. We believe that every discovery has a story, and even the objects left behind on distant worlds deserve to be remembered.

We value curiosity, collaboration, fresh perspectives, and the willingness to learn. Whether you enjoy coding, designing, researching, writing, or bringing ideas to life.
summary: Stellarchive: Far Away from Home is an illustrated storytelling project about the machines that remain on the Moon and Mars after their missions. Through first-person narratives, it brings the journeys of NASA’s Opportunity rover and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles to life. The project explains why these machines were sent, how their tools and mobility systems worked, the challenges they faced, and what they discovered. Opportunity’s exploration revealed evidence that ancient Mars once had water and environments that may have been suitable for microbial life. The Moon buggies helped astronauts travel farther, gather samples, and study lunar geology. By connecting engineering, exploration, and discovery, Stellarchive makes the legacy of human and robotic spaceflight accessible and memorable.
details: Team STELLARCHIVE created Far Away from Home: The Stories of Machines Left Behind in Space, an illustrated educational presentation about NASA’s Opportunity rover on Mars and Apollo’s Lunar Roving Vehicles on the Moon. It works through first-person storytelling and visual explainers to show why the machines were sent, how their tools and mobility systems worked, what challenges they faced, and what they discovered. Opportunity’s findings revealed evidence of ancient Martian water, while the Moon buggies helped astronauts explore farther and collect samples. The project makes space history and planetary science easier to understand, encourages interest in exploration and engineering, and shows how past missions guide future discovery. Its creative feature is giving historic machines a voice and pairing scientific information with visual storytelling. The project was developed as a digital presentation through research, writing, and visual page design. No custom hardware or coding is part of the submitted project.
